items.summary_original: frank kunert makes architecture misbehave in miniature A running track curves around a stadium, except one lane drops into a staircase and disappears below ground. Elsewhere, a narrow apartment is wedged beneath a highway overpass, while a hotel asks its guests to reach their rooms from ladders fixed along the exterior. The German photographer has been building and photographing these small environments since the 1990s. items.summary_original: Calder’s Circus Back in Paris, France One hundred years ago, in 1926, American artist Alexander Calder arrived in Paris. On the occasion of Calder. Rêver en équilibre, at Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris, his foundational project, Cirque Calder (Calder’s Circus), makes a grand return to the European city that defined his career. Teetering, tottering, and fashioned from wire, Calder built this pint-sized circus in the Roaring Twenties. Crouched around the set, about the size of a child’s playset, he would perform the circus for Paris’s avant-garde art scene. items.title: red craft collection reworks four japanese traditional techniques into sculptural domestic objects
items.summary_original: Kenta Yoshizawa turns Japanese crafts into contemporary design Kyoto-based designer Kenta Yoshizawa presents Red Craft (Akai Kogei), a collection that translates traditional Japanese craft techniques and materials into objects for contemporary everyday use. Centered on a vibrant red color palette, the project explores four craft traditions: bamboo fencing, kumihimo braided cord, washi paper , and urushi lacquer, through furniture , lighting , and storage objects. The collection considers how traditional materials and production methods can be integrated into familiar domestic settings while retaining their craft characteristics. Each piece combines functional use with visible references to its material and manufacturing process, creating a connection between traditional Japanese techniques
items.title_de: Die Red Craft Collection verarbeitet vier traditionelle japanische Techniken zu skulpturalen Haushaltsgegenständen
items.summary_de: Kenta Yoshizawa verwandelt japanisches Kunsthandwerk in zeitgenössisches Design. Die in Kyoto ansässige Designerin Kenta Yoshizawa präsentiert Red Craft (Akai Kogei), eine Kollektion, die traditionelle japanische Handwerkstechniken und Materialien in Objekte für den zeitgenössischen Alltagsgebrauch übersetzt. Das Projekt konzentriert sich auf eine leuchtend rote Farbpalette und erforscht vier Handwerkstraditionen: Bambuszäune, geflochtene Kumihimo-Schnüre, Washi-Papier und Urushi-Lack, durch Möbel, Beleuchtung und Aufbewahrungsobjekte. Die Sammlung befasst sich mit der Frage, wie traditionelle Materialien und Produktionsmethoden in vertraute häusliche Umgebungen integriert werden können und gleichzeitig ihre handwerklichen Eigenschaften beibehalten. Jedes Stück kombiniert funktionale Verwendung mit sichtbaren Bezügen zu seinem Material und Herstellungsprozess und schafft so eine Verbindung zwischen traditionellen japanischen Techniken

items.summary_original: Now, if you want to, you can use Google's 3D emoji in your own creations. The company shared some details about how it went about designing the little pictograms and why, as part of World Emoji Day on Friday. Things you might not necessarily worry about in a 2D illustration suddenly become very important when you're talking about a 3D model. Is a smiley face a sphere? A mask? A flat disc? In addition to offering a behind-the-scenes look at Google's design process, it also announced that it would be completely open-sourcing the emoji set: We're handing over raw .OBJ files to the community so they can use them to build immersive VR worlds, … Read the full story at The Verge.

items.title: How Baseline Can Help You Ship Less JavaScript
items.summary_original: Most of us install a dependency once and never look at it again. It does its job, the tests pass, and we move on. But the web platform keeps moving too, and a surprising number of the libraries sitting in your package.json today are now built into the browser. In a typical mid-sized JavaScript app, you can often find somewhere between 60KB and 90KB (minified and gzipped) of dependencies that the platform can now handle on its own. Date and number formatting, HTTP requests, modals, tooltips, deep cloning, grouping arrays: these were all real gaps a few years ago. A lot of them aren’t gaps anymore. Bereits 1883 wurde er gegründet und ist, neben manchem fußballerischen Erfolg, auch bekannt für seine Tribüne, die an einen Friedhof grenzt – und für seine toleranten Fans . Die neue Saison hat er mit einem 2:0 gegen den Favoritner AC eingeläutet – und mit einer Kampagne von Karl Anders . items.title: carlo ratti associati previews a kinetic canopy for modena’s former hospital
items.summary_original: a moving roof arrives in piazza sant’agostino A triangular structure has appeared in Piazza Sant’Agostino, opening and closing in front of the building it will eventually transform. The seven-meter model previews the kinetic roof planned for Italy ‘s AGO Modena Fabbriche Culturali, the vast cultural complex taking shape inside the former Sant’Agostino Hospital. Its three sections draw apart toward the edges of the frame, then gather overhead, turning a mechanical demonstration into a small piece of architecture in its own right. CRA-Carlo Ratti Associati developed the canopy with artist-engineer Chuck Hoberman, whose work has long explored how large structures expand and contract. Corten steel gives the model a weathered outer frame, while stainless steel supports the moving assembly

items.title: What Star Trek got right about AI
items.summary_original: Star Trek imagined talking to a computer decades before the tools arrived to answer. The show’s voice-first computer, plain-language querying, and universal translator anticipated the assistants we ship now — the interface, but not the intelligence. Science fiction tends to be wrong about the future in the ways that matter and right in the ways that don’t. We never got the flying car, but we did get the touchscreen, the video call, and the thing in your pocket that answers questions that happens to be called a phone. Das Design kombiniert eine 3D-gedruckte TPU-Sohle, einen Lederinnenstiefel, der von traditionellen zentralasiatischen Makhsi- und Ichigi-Schuhen inspiriert ist, und ein seilbasiertes Befestigungssystem. Jede Komponente kann getrennt, repariert, ersetzt und recycelt werden, wodurch eine Alternative zur einteiligen Konstruktion geschaffen wird, die üblicherweise bei modernen Turnschuhen verwendet wird. Das Projekt untersucht die Beziehung zwischen traditioneller Handwerkskunst und digitaler Fertigung und nutzt dabei historische Schuhtechniken als Bezugspunkt für einen zirkulären Designansatz. Anstatt sich auf permanente Klebstoffe zu verlassen, die die Reparatur erschweren

items.summary_original: The illustrator talks pencils, party fun, and pitching the perfect box art for Alley Cat Games' What The Sketch? Party games live or die on their box art. Before anyone reads a rule or shuffles a card, they've already decided, in about two seconds, whether the thing on the shelf looks fun. That's a lot of pressure to put on a few illustrated characters and a logo. The game itself is simple: one player becomes the art teacher, describing an object using only basic shapes, while everyone else races to draw and guess what it is. items.title: Gestaltet unsere Birthday Kampagne mit?
items.summary_original: Design is not dead. Creativity is not dead. PAGE is not dead. Und vor allem: Unsere Community ist lebendiger denn je. Was als kreativer Workshop beim Design Camp by PAGE x BECC Agency begann, führen wir jetzt gemeinsam mit euch weiter. Denn die Frage ist: Was ist aus eurer Sicht »not dead«? Seit 40 Jahren begleitet PAGE die Kreativbranche – durch technologische Umbrüche, neue Werkzeuge, veränderte Berufsbilder und immer wieder neue Formen kreativer Zusammenarbeit. Selten hat eine Entwicklung unsere Branche so intensiv beschäftigt wie die Künstliche Intelligenz. Sie eröffnet neue Möglichkeiten, wirft aber auch Fragen auf: Wie verändert sie unseren Beruf? Welche Rolle spielen Kreative künftig? Und was macht unsere Arbeit eigentlich aus? Wir erleben diese Diskussionen jeden Tag – in Redaktion

items.title: CoFo Robert Sans
items.summary_original: Most sans-serifs conform to the mechanical, oversimplified rationality, which can often feel a bit cold. Serif typefaces, on the other hand, achieve their neutrality through traditional, centuries-old calligraphic forms—which are far from soulless. CoFo Robert Sans redefines the concept of a daily sans-serif by using its slab-serif counterpart, CoFo Robert, as its structural foundation. It takes those traditional, warm proportions and translates them into a modern, clean grotesque with a human touch. Its special features are subtle but full of energy: a moderately visible contrast, balanced proportions, and a softness in the curves.
